questions.prompt: BFL's hex guide says hex codes work best when…

options.text: each code is tied to a specific object
options.explanation: Right. The BFL docs say to associate each code with an object or surface, like "the mug in color #FF0000".

options.text: all codes are listed at the very end
options.explanation: BFL's examples put each code next to the object it colours, not in a list at the end.

options.text: the prompt has no colour words at all
options.explanation: BFL's own examples keep colour words, like "deep teal hex #1B6B6F".

questions.prompt: How does Recraft's API take a colour in controls.colors?

options.text: As a hex string, such as "#2E6B4F"
options.explanation: Recraft's colour object has a required rgb field, not a hex string.

options.text: As a colour name, such as "moss green"
options.explanation: Recraft's colour object has a required rgb field, not a name.

options.text: As rgb: three numbers from 0 to 255
options.explanation: Right. Each colour is an rgb list of three integers, with an optional weight.

questions.prompt: The Ideogram docs say Ideogram's JSON color_palette…

options.text: locks every pixel to the listed colours
options.explanation: The Ideogram docs say the colours steer strongly but don't lock every pixel.

options.text: steers colours but does not lock pixels
options.explanation: Right. The Ideogram docs say the colours steer strongly but don't lock every pixel. Check the result with a colour picker.

options.text: only works with lowercase hex codes
options.explanation: Ideogram asks for uppercase #RRGGBB codes, never lowercase.
